original_value: Understanding questions and finding clues for answers are the key for video question answering. Compared with image question answering, video question answering (Video QA) requires to find the clues accurately on both spatial and temporal dimension simultaneously, and thus is more challenging. However, the relationship between spatio-temporal information and question still has not been well utilized in most existing methods for Video QA. To tackle this problem, we propose a Question-Guided Spatio-Temporal Contextual Attention Network (QueST) method. In QueST, we divide the semantic features generated from question into two separate parts: the spatial part and the temporal part, respectively guiding the process of constructing the contextual attention on spatial and temporal dimension. Under the guidance of the corresponding contextual attention, visual features can be better exploited on both spatial and temporal dimensions. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, experiments are conducted on TGIF-QA dataset, MSRVTT-QA dataset and MSVD-QA dataset. Experimental results and comparisons with the state-of-the-art methods have shown that our method can achieve superior performance.

result.paraphrase: In video question answering, the key is to understand questions and identify clues for the answer. Unlike image question answering, Video QA must locate clues accurately in both the spatial and temporal dimensions at the same time, making it more difficult. Yet in most existing Video QA approaches, the relationship between spatio-temporal information and the question remains underused. To address this issue, we introduce a Question-Guided Spatio-Temporal Contextual Attention Network (QueST). QueST splits the semantic features derived from the question into two parts, spatial and temporal, which respectively guide the construction of contextual attention along the spatial and temporal dimensions. With the help of the corresponding contextual attention, visual features can be better leveraged across both dimensions. We evaluate the proposed method on the TGIF-QA, MSRVTT-QA, and MSVD-QA datasets. The experimental results and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance.
